config.prompt: The method's whole strategy is jamming symbol-substitution — file each practice:

items.label: the stored symbol 'eye' — an oval with a circle in it
the beginner's eye is that oval regardless of the model's actual eye
draw the edges at 2 mm per second

config.why: The brain renders the world from priors before the eyes finish reporting — superb for living, terrible for drawing. Once seeing shifts, the same hand produces different drawings; the hand was never the bottleneck.

config.prompt: Pure contour: the hand moves as slowly as the eye. How many millimetres per second is the drill's pace?
config.why: Two millimetres a second, eyes fixed on the object's edge — at that resolution of attention students report edges they had never seen in objects they see daily. Nicolaïdes built his 1941 curriculum on paired extremes: slow contour for observation, fast gesture for vitality.
config.context: about 2 mm/s — ten minutes a day of contour, alternating with gesture, is the smallest viable program

activities.caption: match each measurement to its question
activities.name: obsMeasMatch

config.prompt: Comparative measurement — match each check to its question:

pairs.right: the head fits into the figure how many times? (the standing adult is roughly 7½ heads)
does the knee sit vertically over the ankle? does the ear align with the brow?
the gaps between limbs — unfamiliar shapes the brain cannot correct

config.why: Nobody can draw 'a hand'; everyone can draw angles, widths and alignments — claims verifiable against the subject instead of feelings defended against it.

activities.anchor: most beginner failure is order inversion
activities.caption: the block-in's order of operations
activities.name: obsBlockOrder

config.prompt: Professional drawing is a process with a fixed order — assemble it:
items: Gesture — the quick line of action, 30 seconds
Block-in — largest shapes first, tilts exaggerated so errors show, landmarks placed by measurement
Verification — check alignments and ratios before committing
Value masses — the light/dark pattern in 3–5 values
Detail — features, texture, accents, only where attention should fall
config.why: The economics justify the order: moving a blocked-in shape costs seconds; moving a rendered eye costs the portrait. The Bargue plate course has bootstrapped academy students for 150 years on exactly this discipline.

config.prompt: Two comparison regimes — drag the divider:

before.label: sight-size
before.text: subject and drawing side by side at identical scale from one fixed standing point — compared directly at the same retinal scale, no mental translation; the costs: slow, rigid, the head must not drift

after.label: freer comparative methods
after.text: pencil-and-thumb units from any viewpoint — spontaneous and mobile; the price: every comparison runs through mental translation

config.why: The deal: sight-size trains the eye's calibration; freer methods are for working life — 'the drawing's shoulder reads wider than the model's' is a correction you can act on immediately.

activities.caption: sequence your subjects — what comes first?
activities.name: obsSubjBranch

config.root: You are sequencing your own training and can pick the next subject. The lesson's progression has reasons — run it:

start.text: Which subject do you start with, and why?

choices.label: Still life — it does not move, its geometry is knowable, you own the lighting
choices.feedback: The laboratory: still life is where the method is calibrated before any psychology arrives.

choices.label: Portrait — the face's expressiveness first
choices.feedback: That is the psychology problem — every symbol-library error tempts there, and no two noses obey the same template. It comes after the calibration.

choices.label: Figure — the everything problem
choices.feedback: Moving, three-dimensional, proportioned and alive — where gesture, anatomy and observation meet. The last step, not the first.

still.text: Knowable geometry, owned lighting, a subject that holds still — the right first rung.

portrait.text: Subtle symmetries and individual faces — the second rung, once measurement is a habit.

figure.text: The everything problem — the rung that assumes all the others.

config.why: Still life first, portrait next, figure last — and alongside the sequence, primary observation stays the irreplaceable source, with photographs and master studies as knowingly-used secondary sources.

config.text: Memory drawing: observe, look away, draw from memory, then check — the gap between remembered and seen is a map of your %%0%%. Plein air: light changes the value structure every %%1%%, so the drill forces decisions, commitment and value-first thinking.
config.hint: One is what the gap reveals; one is the clock the outdoors runs on.

activities.caption: one line of this sketchbook doctrine is wrong
activities.name: obsBookSpot

config.prompt: One line of this sketchbook doctrine is wrong — click it:
lines: Thumbnail sketch — postage-stamp value-and-shape studies testing a composition in ninety seconds.
Quick sketch — one to five minutes, capturing pose, proportion and character.
Sustained study — the measured block-in at full attention, where understanding is built.
Frame and exhibit every page — a sketchbook's pages are finished work.
Workflow: sketch to collect, thumbnails to compose, studies to understand, then the final piece executes decisions already made.
config.correction: The sketchbook is a working record — the slow seeing happens on pages nobody will frame, which is why finished work arrives fast months later.
config.why: Thumbnail, quick sketch and sustained study are field instruments — cheap failures, chosen successes — and the workflow explains the professional asymmetry beginners find mystifying.
